response: Yes, unicompartmental knee replacement (UKR) can restore normal knee kinematics in many patients. UKR is a surgical procedure that replaces only the damaged compartment of the knee, preserving the healthy compartments and ligaments. By doing so, it can help maintain the natural movement and function of the knee, allowing for more normal kinematics compared to total knee replacement. However, the extent of kinematic restoration may vary depending on factors such as the severity of pre-operative deformity, surgical technique, and implant design.
